newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia sells EastSiberian Oil/Gas stake to unknown.
newsitem.headline: Russia sells EastSiberian Oil/Gas stake to unknown.

text.p: Russia has sold a 47 percent stake to an unknown buyer in the East Siberian Oil and Gas Company, which has estimated oil reserves of 702.7 million tonnes, the Federal Securities Corporation said on Monday.
The Corporation did not say who had bought the stake in Vostochno-Sibirskaya Neftegazovaya Kompaniya, which sold for 46.51 billion roubles ($8.2 million).
The sale in the independent oil firm took place December 30, 1996, but the Corporation released results only on Monday.

The stake was sold in two lots -- a 32 percent stake of 5,480,400 shares, for 35.73 billion roubles or 6,520 roubles per share, and a 15 percent stake of 2,567,061 shares, for 10.8 billion roubles or 4,200 roubles per share.
The starting price was 1,400 roubles per share.
The government holds a 38 percent stake, post-auction, in the company. A 15 percent stake was sold in small blocks at a 1995 auction.

East Siberian has two subsidiaries, Yeniseigeofizika and Yeniseineftegaz. The latter won a January 1996 auction to develop the Yurubchenskaya oil field with Russian estimated oil reserves of 702.7 million tonnes in Siberia's Krasnoyarsk region.
